question:
**Direction: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

I couldn't understand why he was **__so angry upon me__**.
solution:
The correct answer is **'so angry with me.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If directed at a person, **"angry with"** should always be used. (यदि किसी व्यक्ति पर निर्देशित किया जाता है तो हमेशा "angry with" का उपयोग किया जाना चाहिए)​

 
 
• **Example**: *I was very** angry with** her.*
 
 
 
• Hence, the preposition 'upon' should be replaced by the preposition 'with' to make the sentence grammatically correct. (इसलिए, वाक्य को व्याकरणिक रूप से सही बनाने के लिए preposition 'upon' को preposition 'with' द्वारा प्रतिस्थापित किया जाना चाहिए)

 

​Correct sentence__:* **I couldn't understand why he was __**so angry with me**__.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** *

 
• There are three articles: *a, an, and the.*

 
 
• Indefinite article 'an': before a singular noun beginning with a vowel sound whose specific identity is not known.
 
• Definite article 'the': before a singular or plural noun whose specific identity is known.
 
• Indefinite article 'a': before a singular noun beginning with a consonant sound whose specific identity is not known.
